paragraphs: Friend, here's what this parable teaches. God is patient, and He keeps reaching out. The owner doesn't give up after one servant. He sends a second, then a third, and then he says, "I will send my beloved son." That's a picture of how far God goes to reach people, and it matters because you are one of the people He's reaching for (Luke 20:10-13).

But the tenants had a problem, and it's a problem we can all have. They treated the vineyard like it was theirs. They were only renters, and they acted like owners! When a tenant starts saying "the inheritance will be ours," something has gone sideways (Luke 20:14). Jesus is showing that everything we have is lent to us, and the One who owns it gets to ask for His share. Hearing that stings a little, I know, and the people said, "May such a thing never happen!" (Luke 20:16).

Then Jesus looks right at them and points to the stone: "The stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone" (Luke 20:17). Rejecting Him doesn't take away His place, because God has already set Him as the cornerstone. So the question for you is a simple one, friend. Will you build on that stone, or trip over it (Luke 20:18)? Build on Him, and I promise the foundation holds, even when your own batch comes out lopsided.
